Working from the article text provided directly.

---

**Published online:**
September 4, 2026 (Reuters)

**Geographic focus:**
Global — primary focus on US, Eurozone, Japan; secondary mention of Australia, UK, Senegal/West Africa

**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical report [NO]
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES]

**Synopsis:**
A global bond market selloff is pushing yields to multi-year or multi-decade highs across the US, Europe, Japan, and Australia. Key near-term catalysts include US PPI and CPI data, the Fed's September 15–16 meeting (roughly 50/50 odds on a hike), and an ECB meeting expected to deliver a 25bps hike. Japan is central to the story — 10-year JGB yields above 3% for the first time in 30 years, raising fears of Japanese capital repatriation from foreign bond markets. The yen surged ~3% in two sessions. The US Treasury announced expanded buybacks of longer-dated debt. Fed Governor Waller signaled a hold preference if inflation data cooperates. Senegal's IMF debt restructuring adds an EM tail risk. Oracle earnings may refocus attention on the AI trade.

---

**Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?**
Relevance: YES — US CPI/PPI data, the Fed's September meeting odds, Treasury buyback operations, and US yield dynamics are all central to the article.

**Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?**
Relevance: 70 (moderately-high; a Fed hike at the Sept 15–16 meeting is actively debated, with Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech tilting markets toward a hike)
Probability of increase: 50%

**Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?**
Relevance: 65 (Fed Governor Waller explicitly signaled inclination to hold if incoming inflation data confirms cooling; this counterbalances the hike narrative)
Probability of holding: 50%

**Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?**
Relevance: 5 (cuts are not discussed; the entire framing is hike-or-hold, with bond yields surging)
Probability of decrease: 0%

**Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?**
Sentiment: +15 (Slightly hawkish, but pulling back from peak hawkishness — Warsh's Jackson Hole speech pushed markets toward pricing a hike, but Waller's subsequent dovish lean and roughly 50/50 market pricing leave the net tone only modestly hawkish heading into the September meeting)
